## Purpose

Inventory an intended root cutover and print its ordered operator steps before
changing GitHub settings or AQ bindings.

## When a playbook uses it

A local operator or live elevated supervisor inspects readiness, settles named
holders and reviews which aborted inputs become eligible on the new default.

## How it works internally

`src/integration/cutover.py` reads repository-scoped subjects, owners, legacy
intents and open train batches, cadence policy, retained completion provenance,
aborted members, scoped data-fix IDs, root OID, open PRs and current GitHub policy.
It verifies the delivered workflow's PR branch coverage and prints each blocker.

## Side effects and persistence

The command reads Git, PostgreSQL and GitHub without publishing branches or
changing configuration. Save its JSON before manual GitHub changes; apply uses
that snapshot to detect changed bindings, inputs and data-fix rows.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

Missing repository identity, unavailable Git/GitHub observations or an invalid
flow refuse the read. A returned plan can contain blockers: resolve the named
controls and preview again before changing remote policy. `--allow-epics` permits
live epic collection while preserving the root and flow-target barriers.

## Example step

Save a plan from the operator CLI:

```bash
aq integration cutover-plan --project demo --flow promotion-flow.yaml > cutover.json
```

Use `--reverse` to inspect the recorded inverse. The
[runbook](../../guides/git-first-train-runbook.md#moving-the-root-to-a-promotion-flow-source)
describes the manual restoration and apply sequence.
